matches.rationale: No finding identifies the abstract's overstatement of 4.2× TTFT reduction and 3.2–4.5× throughput relative to the experimental figures. The discrepancy reported in pred_id 1 involves different (much higher) numbers and a different cross-section inconsistency.

Exactly matches: pred_id 5 identifies the contradiction in Section 3.1 where prose defines burst tolerance as a difference-based normalization while Equation (1) uses a ratio, which is the same logical inconsistency.
No finding mentions the missing baseline configuration details (batch sizes, KV cache settings, DistServe extension specifics) that undermine the experimental protocol.
Pred_id 3 notes that Section 4.2 claims up to 4.5× and 3.2× throughput over vLLM while Figure 6 values do not support those ratios, which is the same evidence-inflation error.

Pred_id 13 identifies the unsupported universal claim about applicability to 'all MLLM architectures, including cross-attention, prefix-tuning, and adapter-based models,' matching the overgeneralization based on only two model architectures.
Pred_id 12 directly reports the non-existent citation [61] for 'Zhang et al. … proposed a similar two-tier separation in 2024,' which is the exact fabricated reference called out in the ground truth.
No finding discusses the undefined penalty factor β or the inconsistent swap from decode (B_d) to prefill (R'_p) in Equation 3.
No finding raises the omission of ethical considerations (user consent, IRB, terms of service) regarding the datasets.

No finding identifies the promotional claim in the Introduction that ElasticMM 'completely eliminates all inference bottlenecks.' Pred_id 14 concerns the Conclusion's overstatement, not the Introduction.
No finding points out the narrative misalignment where the abstract lists unified multimodal prefix caching as part of EMP despite it being a separate Section 3.3 optimization.
No finding addresses the ablation study claim that both optimizations provide 'roughly equal' gains when Figure 8 likely shows an imbalance.
No finding mentions the unfair comparison where ElasticMM was allegedly tested with custom CUDA kernels and memory allocators unavailable to baselines.
Pred_id 13 explicitly flags the Conclusion's unsupported claim of SLO compliance 'under all workload conditions,' which distorts the conditional experimental results in the same way.
No finding mentions the fabricated historical lineage attributing encoder-decoder MLLM architecture to Vaswani et al. [10].

No finding identifies the omission of limitation statements and negative societal impact discussions. Pred_id 14 attacks a positive claim of no limitations rather than the omission of such discussion.
